radome.description: The dielectric radar nose, ahead of the cockpit. Four tapered charts wrap its left, underside, right and top quadrants. This is smooth composite, not a sheet-metal patchwork. Only the attachment rim at the wide aft end has a fine joint. No rivet grid across the composite. Very faint longitudinal cleaning traces, no metal scratches.
radome.neighbor_method: four closest canonical part centroids; context states actual construction where known

forward_left.description: The left forward fuselage side below the cockpit, between the radome and intake. Forward is toward the radome. The closed gun-port panel is an avionics access cover, no gun opening. Frame stations support circumferential fastener rows, not a dense rectangular greeble grid. Leave clean stencil zones under the cockpit sill; decals come later. The canopy sill is above this sheet, the intake is aft.
forward_left.neighbor_method: four closest canonical part centroids; context states actual construction where known

wing_root.description: The upper inboard wing root and strake, joining the left fuselage fillet to the main upper wing. A narrow curved sheet, not an entire triangular wing. The yellow guide zone indicates a restrained antislip walkway near the fuselage. It is a subtle grey material change with soft shoe scuffs, no black racing stripe or text. Blue structural lines follow the actual spars and ribs. Outboard it meets the upper wing.
wing_root.neighbor_method: four closest canonical part centroids; context states actual construction where known

wing_upper.description: Two upper wing charts: inboard cranked panel and outboard fixed wing box. The smaller tip panel starts beyond the planform crank. The leading-edge flap, trailing flap and aileron are separate parts, absent from these islands. Their cut edges are real hinge boundaries, not extra access covers. Follow the two spars and actual rib stations. Keep a small fuel filler within the tank box, between the spars and outboard of the crank, diameter about 0.11 m. No walkway outboard.
wing_upper.neighbor_method: four closest canonical part centroids; context states actual construction where known

fin_left.description: Left face of the vertical fin, its lower root fillet and small top cap, above the rear fuselage. The rudder is a separate trailing control surface and is absent. Use a fine perimeter joint near that cut boundary, a few flush fasteners near the base and one restrained root service cover. No invented fin spar grid: the current model has no separate fin spar layout exported here. Keep broad skin clean. Generated detail is reflected in aircraft world coordinates to the other face; the compositor adds readable separate fin markings.
fin_left.neighbor_method: four closest canonical part centroids; context states actual construction where known

selection_policy: world positions and normals within named physical parts; chart indices never establish identity
registration_contract: groups[].generation_atlas_charts belong to the source atlas; current masks contain mapped ownership and are not native chart registration inputs
limitations: New and replaced doors and speed brakes use nearest accepted parent paint, not new generated structural detail.
Brake wells and actuators on jet_mechanical are outside the skin atlas and retain their mechanical material.
Native IoU and density gates run on preserved generation-atlas charts; world reuse is measured separately.
